setup: Sit upright on a flat or low-back bench, or stand with feet hip-width apart and a braced core.
Hoist a single dumbbell overhead using both hands, forming a diamond or heart-shaped cup with your palms flat against the inside face of the upper weight plate.
Position your upper arms vertically alongside your ears with elbows pointing forward and upward.
steps: Inhale and lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending at the elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Descend until your forearms pass parallel to the floor or you feel a deep, comfortable stretch in your triceps.
Exhale and press the dumbbell back up by extending your elbows to return to the starting position without locking out abruptly.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower the weight behind your head; exhale forcefully as you extend your elbows to press back overhead.
cues: Keep elbows tucked forward, not flared out wide
Lock your upper arms in place and move only the forearms
Brace your abs to prevent arching your lower back

common_faults.correction: Keep elbows pointing predominantly forward to optimize triceps recruitment and reduce shoulder joint strain.

common_faults.fault: Excessive lumbar hyperextension to compensate for shoulder mobility.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core, contract the glutes, or perform the exercise on a bench with back support.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the upper arms back and forth to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Fix the upper arms vertically beside your head and isolate movement strictly to elbow flexion and extension.

precautions: Ensure a secure two-handed grip on the underside of the dumbbell plate before hoisting it overhead.
Use a manageable load to avoid striking the back of the neck or losing control overhead.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension
summary: An isolation exercise that targets the triceps, particularly the long head, by extending the elbow from a fully stretched overhead position.
